title: Compass steps on a letter grid: king distance, distinct moves and compass-line moves of the 24 clue pairs on 14.5M grids
k4_result: 0 of 14,541,780 K4 grids (98 small-set + 220,232 dictionary alphabets x widths 3-13 x 26/27 cells x flat/cwrap/twrap) give R = 1 (every clue pair a compass step); chance expectation 7.7e-6. Best R = 2 (small set: 2 grids; dictionary: ~5,700 per third). 0 grids with D <= 8 (best D = 12 small set, 9 dictionary). Best Q = 22 (small) and 24 (dictionary). Block 1 alone: 620 R=1 grids on the dictionary (0 on the small set), all at width 3 with wrapped columns, where a compass step is a letter shift of -4..+4 on a near-A-Z keyword alphabet: this is Bean's known closeness of the EASTNORTHEAST letters, not a grid effect. Block 2 alone: 2 R=1 grids on the small set (VALLEYOFTHEKINGS w3 twrap), 0 on the dictionary.
controls: 200 shuffled K4s on the small set: best R 2 (160) or 3 (40), K4 2 (share as extreme 0.80); best D 10-13, K4 12 (0.95); best Q 20-23, K4 22 (0.45); R=1 grids 0 in all 200. 3 shuffled K4s on a third of the dictionary each: best R 2, D 9/10/8, Q 23/24/24, R=1 grids 0 (one shuffle has 2 grids with D <= 8, K4 0). Block 1 alone R=1: shuffles 0/0/0 on the dictionary thirds vs K4 184/188/248 (the Bean closeness effect, which shuffling destroys). Block 2 alone R=1: shuffles 8/8/0 vs K4 0/0/0 on the dictionary; small set 1 of 200 shuffles has 4, K4 2 (p = 0.005, one of ~15 statistics looked at, and reversed on the dictionary).
planted: 3/3 found with R = 1 at the planted grid (KRYPTOS w7 flat, UNDERGROUND w5 flat, PALIMPSEST w9 27 cells both wraps); read back 54, 68, 50 of 97 letters vs 35, 35, 32.5 for a random choice among the candidates. The plan's bar of 60/97 was met by 1 of 3: with 9 plain candidates per letter, an exact quadgram Viterbi plus word split tops out at about 54/97 on average (tested on 12 plants), so the reading stage is weaker than hoped; the exact R = 1 test is unaffected.
scope_limits: Alphabets only from A-Z, KRYPTOS, 84 theme-word keyword alphabets, 12 old-script orders and 220,232 dictionary keyword alphabets (no transposition-mixed forms, no free hidden alphabet). Grids filled row by row, widths 3-13, '?' only as the 27th (last) cell. Moves measured as the shortest move under each convention; no rule for the move sequence is assumed. Moves of 2 or more cells cannot be judged (in grids of width >= 9 with row wrap, or width 13 flat, row moves are always within 1, so those grids are weak tests). The reading stage reads back only about 55/97 of a planted text, so a real R = 1 survivor would need a human read; none arose.

negative.hypothesis: With the alphabet written in a grid, each K4 cipher letter is one compass step (N, NE, ... or stay) from its plain letter, so all 24 clue pairs are king moves apart on the right grid.
negative.scope: A-Z, KRYPTOS, 84 theme, 12 old-script and 220,232 dictionary keyword alphabets; rows of width 3-13; 26 cells or 27 with '?' last; no wrap, columns wrap, both wrap; statistics R (largest king distance), D (distinct moves), Q (moves on compass lines), all 24 pairs and each clue block alone.
negative.outcome: Dead: 0 of 14.5M grids give R = 1 or D <= 8 on all 24 clue pairs; best R = 2, D = 9, Q = 24, same as shuffled K4s (200 on the small set, 3 on dictionary thirds: R 2, D 8-13, Q 20-24). Block-1-only hits (620) are all width-3 wrapped grids = Bean's known small-shift effect. Planted 3/3 found with R = 1.

follow_ups: Free hidden alphabet: decide exactly whether ANY arrangement of 26 letters in a w-wide grid makes all 24 clue pairs king moves (a graph-embedding / backtracking test like idea 112's window solver), which the listed alphabets cannot settle.
